summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission after bone marrow transplant, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 11%, chronic graft-versus-host disease, and advanced kidney disease, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and worsening dyspnea. He was found to have Clostridioides difficile infection causing diarrhea, a gout flare in his right foot, and acute on chronic kidney failure with a creatinine of 6.2 mg/dL. Due to persistent symptoms and fluid overload despite dobutamine, he was initiated on hemodialysis following placement of a tunneled dialysis catheter. His symptoms improved with treatment, including vancomycin for C. diff, a prednisone taper for gout, and dialysis for volume and uremic management. He was discharged home on home oxygen, with outpatient dialysis scheduled three times weekly, and instructions to complete his medications and monitor weight.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
